findings.reason: Case mismatch: the accusative object 'çıktıyı' does not agree with 'ince ayar yapın' (which requires the dative 'çıktıya'); a native speaker would write 'ince ayarlayın'.
The English adjective 'quantized' is left untranslated in Turkish text; a Turkish equivalent (e.g. 'nicemlenmiş' / 'kuantize edilmiş') should be used since 'quantized' is not a protected proper noun.
Same untranslated English adjective 'quantized' carried into the FAQ answer; should use a Turkish term.

findings.suggestion: görseller oluşturması gereken kullanıcılar için özellikle faydalıdır
findings.reason: English says 'users who need to create images'; translation generalizes 'images' to 'içerikler' (content) and softens 'need' to 'want'.
The English says resolutions up to 4K at 50fps; the Turkish attaches '50fps' directly to 'çözünürlük', reading as '50fps resolution', which is awkward/imprecise.
'Load ... workflow' corresponds to the app term 'İş Akışını Yükle'; 'açın' (open) deviates from the established UI wording.

findings.span: metin girişini işleyerek video içerik üretir
findings.suggestion: metin girişini işleyerek video içeriği üretir
findings.reason: Missing possessive/compound suffix: 'video içeriği' is the correct Turkish noun compound.
English says 'Load the workflow'; 'açın' means 'open'. The app term for Load Workflow is 'İş Akışını Yükle', so 'yükleyin' matches the UI better.
The source consistently wraps node names in single quotes ('LoadImage', 'SaveVideo'); the quotes around this node name were dropped, making formatting inconsistent within the same paragraph.

The ComfyUI UI term 'Bypass' has a required Turkish rendering ('Atla'); the untranslated verb 'bypass edin' does not match the app terminology.
Same UI term inconsistency: 'Bypass' should follow the required app translation 'Atla'.

'client reviews' means review/feedback sessions, not approvals ('onaylar').

findings.suggestion: basit çizgilerle ve kare başına açıklamalarla tek bir 6 panelli siyah-beyaz eskiz board'u üretir
findings.reason: Omits 'with simple lines' from the English description of the output.
'Queue Prompt' is a ComfyUI UI button and must use the required Turkish translation 'İstemi Kuyruğa Al' so the page matches the app.
Inconsistent terminology within the same entry: 'frame' is rendered as 'kare' elsewhere (extendedDescription 'kareler', FAQ 'kare aralığı').
'prompt' is left in English throughout extendedDescription and howToUse but translated as 'istem' here; the page should use one consistent term.
The same control is referred to as 'edit strength' (untranslated) in extendedDescription and howToUse; inconsistent naming of the same parameter across the page.
Mixing the English verb 'decode' with Turkish morphology reads as unpolished in published copy; a native Turkish equivalent exists.

findings.reason: Awkward construction: it literally says 'update the latest version of ComfyUI'. The object of the verb should be ComfyUI, with the latest version as the target; also 'as per the guide' becomes 'with the guide'.
'specificity' is rendered as 'açıklık' (clarity), duplicating 'netlik' and losing the distinct meaning of being specific.

findings.suggestion: XML istemlerle detaylı anime görselleri için ... keşfedin

The English says 'introducing realistic motion'; the comparative 'daha' (more) is an addition not present in the source.
'static image' is rendered 'sabit görsel' in the description, metaDescription and howToUse but 'durağan görsel' here; terminology should be consistent across the page.
'powerful tool' is weakened to 'solid/robust tool'.

findings.suggestion: Skin Enhancer + Upscaler (or use the same form consistently across all fields)
findings.reason: The workflow name is translated in the title and extendedDescription but left in English in metaDescription and howToUse, so the same workflow is referred to by two different names on one page.
English says 'in under 60 seconds'; the translation drops 'under' and states the exact duration, unlike the description field which renders it correctly.

findings.suggestion: Use one verb for 'upscale' across the entry (preferably 'yükseltme/yükseltmek', matching the ComfyUI term for upscaling)
findings.reason: 'upscale' is rendered as 'yükseltmek' here but as 'büyütmek' in the title, description and extendedDescription; inconsistent terminology within the same entry.
'geçiş' means transition and is not natural Turkish for UI 'toggles'; a native speaker would say 'anahtar' or 'aç/kapat düğmesi'.
'Ekle' means 'Add', while the English is 'Apply'; the body text consistently uses 'doku uygulamak' (apply texture), so the title is slightly inconsistent with the rest of the entry.
Turkish orthography does not use a comma directly before the conjunction 've' in a list.

findings.span: GeminiImage2Node ile doku ayarlarını optimize edin.
findings.suggestion: En iyi sonuçlar için GeminiImage2Node ile doku ayarlarını düzenleyin.
findings.reason: The English instructs to adjust settings 'for optimal results'; the translation converts this into 'optimize the settings', dropping the purpose clause and changing the action.
Hyphenated construction 'video-dan-videoya' is not idiomatic Turkish orthography; suffixes should be attached without hyphens.
'kesinti' means interruption/outage; the English 'hard cuts' refers to editing cuts ('kesme/kesim').

Unnecessary English loanword 'upscale' where the rest of the page consistently uses the Turkish 'büyüt-' (e.g. 'görseli büyütür', 'büyütülür').
'altyazı' means video subtitles; the source refers to an image captioning node, so the term conveys the wrong function.

VFX 'plate' is rendered as 'plaka' (which in Turkish means license/metal plate) here and in metaDescription, but as 'plate' in extendedDescription and suggestedUseCases; the page is inconsistent and 'plaka' is misleading in a VFX context.
Same 'plate' term inconsistency as the description; extendedDescription and use cases keep 'plate'.
'frame' is left in English here while the same paragraph and the FAQ use the Turkish 'kare' ('kareleri çıkarır', 'kare başına', 'kare sayısı'); inconsistent within the entry.
Missing instrumental case; 'yeşil doldurulur' is ungrammatical for 'green-filled'.

'feather' is left in English here but translated as 'tüy' in the FAQ answer ('tüy yarıçapını'); inconsistent terminology within the entry.

"keyframe" and "finalize" are left in English although the body consistently uses "ana kare" and Turkish verbs; inconsistent register within the same entry.

findings.suggestion: Uzattıkça kalite ve sahne tutarlılığı genellikle azalır

The workflow name is translated in the title field but left in English here, creating an inconsistency across the page.
"Dailies" is a film-industry term for the raw footage shot each day; "prodüksiyon günlükleri" reads as production logs/diaries, which is a different thing.

findings.span: Klipinizi almak için LoadVideo ile başlar
findings.suggestion: Klibinizi almak için LoadVideo ile başlar
findings.reason: Turkish consonant mutation: "klip" + possessive/accusative becomes "klibinizi", not "klipinizi" (the howToUse section correctly uses "klibi").
Vowel harmony error: "LoRA" ends in a back vowel, so the accusative suffix should be "-yı", not "-yi".
Inconsistent terminology across the page: "inpainting" is rendered as "boyama" here and in howToUse, but left as "inpainting" in extendedDescription and the FAQ answers.

findings.span: Eğer açıksa, filigran kaldırma ile doku koruma arasında denge kurmak için
findings.suggestion: Eğer bu ayar gösteriliyorsa, filigran kaldırma ile ince doku korumasi arasında denge kurmak için
findings.reason: "If exposed" means "if the parameter is surfaced in the node UI"; "Eğer açıksa" reads as "if it is open/enabled". Also "fine" in "fine texture retention" is dropped.
Inconsistent with the FAQ, which keeps "denoise gücü"; additionally "gürültü azaltma" suggests a noise-reduction filter rather than the diffusion denoise strength parameter.

"dizi" means array/series, while "dize" is the correct Turkish term for a text string; the same source term is rendered as "ön ayar dizelerini" later in the same field, so the entry is internally inconsistent.

findings.reason: "inputs prepared upstream" refers to earlier nodes in the pipeline; "girişte hazırlanan parametreleri" changes 'inputs' to 'parameters' and loses the upstream notion.

findings.span: Gerekirse seçili ön ayarı veya metin parametrelerini değiştirip tekrar çalıştırın.
findings.suggestion: Gerekirse seçili ön ayarı veya metin parametrelerini değiştirip görünümü beğenene kadar tekrar çalıştırın.
findings.reason: Omits 'until you're happy with the look' from the source sentence.

Incorrect Turkish genitive suffix on a word ending in a vowel; should take the buffer -n- and follow vowel harmony with the final /i/ sound (ComfyUI'nin), consistent with other uses like 'ComfyUI'yi' / 'ComfyUI'ye'.
Incorrect Turkish possessive suffix on the proper noun; ComfyUI is treated as vowel-final elsewhere (e.g. 'ComfyUI'yi', 'ComfyUI'ye'), so the genitive should be 'ComfyUI'nin'.
Missing possessive/buffer consonant: 'matris' takes the dative 'matrisine' in this construction; 'matrise' reads as ungrammatical here.
Untranslated English marketing terms left inline; these are not proper nouns and a Turkish reader would expect localized wording.

findings.reason: 'çağrı-aksiyon' is not idiomatic Turkish for 'call-to-action'; standard renderings are 'eylem çağrısı' or 'harekete geçirici mesaj'.
'blur' is an untranslated English common noun; Turkish 'bulanıklık' is standard and consistent with the rest of the text.
